subject: Question regarding the range of the dynamic covariates

messages.author: 28c4bdfcd7324d44
messages.subject: Question regarding the range of the dynamic covariates
parts:
Hello,

I would like to ask if there is a way in which we can restrict the range of a model's covariates.
I mean, suppose that we are running a simple regression and we know that there is a (strong) positive correlation among the response y and a covariate x (under, let's say, an AR1 model) 
Is there any way with which we can assure that x's path will always stay positive?

Thank you in advance,
Maria

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Question regarding the range of the dynamic covariates
parts:
On Mon, 2015-08-31 at 13:22 -0700, Maria Skoularidou wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I would like to ask if there is a way in which we can restrict the
> range of a model's covariates.
> I mean, suppose that we are running a simple regression and we know
> that there is a (strong) positive correlation among the response y
> and a covariate x (under, let's say, an AR1 model)
> Is there any way with which we can assure that x's path will always
> stay positive?

Hi,

only for single variables this is possible, like beta*x where
beta\in[a,b], is possible (model="clinear")

for higher dimensional models, like

f(time, x, model="ar1")

this is not possible. sorry.
